subtitle: Ahmadullah Shah and the Trap at Chinhat

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle battlefield wide at dawn
panels.action: Ahmadullah Shah stands resolute on a dusty rise near Chinhat, arm raised toward lines of rebel horse and infantry as British guns glint in the distance under a smoky June sky.

dialogue.text: June 1857, Awadh: Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah of Faizabad will lure Henry Lawrence into Chinhat’s trap, win a rare open-field victory, and pay for it with his head at Powayan.

i18n.hi: जून 1857, अवध: फैज़ाबाद के मौलवी अहमदुल्लाह शाह हेनरी लॉरेंस को चिनहट के फंदे में खींचेंगे, मैदान में दुर्लभ जीत पाएँगे, और पवाँयां में सिर गँवाएँगे।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a crowded mosque-court in Faizabad
panels.action: Ahmadullah Shah, robed and turbaned, stands on a simple platform in Faizabad, one hand resting on a Qur’an, the other gesturing outward to a packed courtyard of sepoys, townsmen, and taluqdar retainers.

dialogue.text: In Faizabad, before Chinhat, Ahmadullah Shah was already a name: a traveling Maulvi who mixed scriptural authority with the hard craft of organizing men.

i18n.hi: चिनहट से पहले ही फैज़ाबाद में अहमदुल्लाह शाह मशहूर थे: घूमने वाले मौलवी, जो धर्म की ताकत को लोगों को संगठित करने की सख्त कला से मिलाते थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in close on his intense, weathered face
panels.action: Close on Ahmadullah Shah’s face, eyes sharp, beard neatly kept, as he leans forward, speaking quietly yet firmly to a circle of Awadh leaders seated before him.

dialogue.speaker: ahmadullah_shah
dialogue.text: If we fight alone, we fall alone. Awadh must rise together.

i18n.hi: अकेले लड़ेंगे तो अकेले गिरेंगे। अवध को मिलकर उठना होगा।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of Awadh countryside with marching bands of men
panels.action: From above, dusty tracks wind through fields and mango groves as small bands of sepoys and retainers converge on Faizabad, some touching greeting hands with Ahmadullah Shah’s followers.

dialogue.text: When the revolt flared in May and June, he moved across Awadh, drawing sepoys, townsmen, and taluqdar forces into a loose, shared cause against Company rule.

i18n.hi: मई–जून में बगावत भड़की तो वो अवध भर घूमे, सिपाहियों, शहरियों और तालुकेदारों को कंपनी के खिलाफ एक ढीली, साझा लड़ाई में जोड़ते गए।

panels.shot: interior wide of the Lucknow Residency map room
panels.action: Inside the dim map room of the Lucknow Residency, Henry Lawrence bends over a large table, British officers around him, as a messenger points at the road to Chinhat on a marked map.

dialogue.text: In Lucknow, Henry Lawrence read alarmed reports: Ahmadullah’s men were gathering on the road to Chinhat, threatening the fragile hold on the Residency.

i18n.hi: लखनऊ में हेनरी लॉरेंस घबराए हुए रिपोर्ट पढ़ रहा था: अहमदुल्लाह के लोग चिनहट की सड़क पर जुट रहे थे, रेज़िडेंसी पर लगी कमजोर पकड़ हिल रही थी।

panels.shot: medium shot on Henry Lawrence in uniform, resolute
panels.action: Henry Lawrence, weary but determined in British uniform, stands by a window overlooking the Residency courtyard, jaw set as sepoys and loyalist troops assemble below.

dialogue.text: On 30 June 1857, Lawrence chose what many saw as a gamble: to march out at dawn with a small column and break the rebel force in open country.

i18n.hi: 30 जून 1857 को लॉरेंस ने वो कदम चुना जिसे कई लोग जुआ मानते थे: भोर में छोटी टुकड़ी लेकर निकलना और खुले मैदान में बगावतियों को तोड़ देना।

panels.shot: long shot of the British column moving out at dawn
panels.action: The British-led column of infantry, cavalry, and guns snakes out of the Residency gate at first light, wheels creaking, dust rising, as the domes and minarets of Lucknow recede behind.

dialogue.text: About eight hundred men, with guns, rode toward Chinhat. Few knew how many waited for them, or how well that ground had been studied from the other side.

i18n.hi: करीब आठ सौ जवान, तोपों के साथ, चिनहट की तरफ चले। कम ही लोगों को पता था सामने कितने हैं, या दूसरी तरफ से उस ज़मीन को कितना तौला गया है।

panels.shot: wide shot of rebel camp near Chinhat with prepared positions
panels.action: Near the village of Chinhat, Ahmadullah Shah surveys positioned guns behind low embankments, cavalry massed on flanks, infantry crouched along the road, the morning sun glinting off matchlocks and sabers.

dialogue.text: Ahmadullah Shah and allied leaders had chosen the ground carefully. According to British accounts, he placed guns and horse with a soldier’s eye, turning Chinhat into a waiting snare.

i18n.hi: अहमदुल्लाह शाह और उसके साथी सरदारों ने मैदान सोच–समझकर चुना था। अंग्रेज़ी बयान के मुताबिक उसने तोप और घुड़सवार सैनिक की नज़र से बैठाए, चिनहट को घात की घाटी बना दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot side-on as he gives crisp orders
panels.action: Ahmadullah Shah points toward the road, speaking to a group of rebel officers, while messengers sprint away and horsemen tighten girths, the tension thick in the humid June air.

dialogue.speaker: ahmadullah_shah
dialogue.text: Let them come forward. Hit the guns first, then cut off their road.

i18n.hi: उन्हें आगे आने दो। पहले तोपों पर वार, फिर उनकी राह काटो।

panels.shot: dynamic battlefield wide as the British column meets sudden fire
panels.action: The British column, stretched along the road, reels as rebel guns flash from the flanks; smoke billows, horses rear, and Ahmadullah Shah watches from a rise, reading the chaos.

dialogue.text: Near Chinhat, the trap sprang. Rebel guns and cavalry struck from the sides, the road turned into a funnel, and Lawrence’s column began to break under the sudden weight.

i18n.hi: चिनहट के पास जाल खुल गया। बगावती तोपें और घुड़सवार किनारों से टूट पड़े, सड़क सुरंग बन गई और अचानक दबाव में लॉरेंस की टुकड़ी बिखरने लगी।

panels.shot: low-angle on rebel cavalry charge commanded from the rear
panels.action: Rebel cavalry surge forward in a sweeping charge, dust cloaking their rush, as Ahmadullah Shah remains slightly back, hand raised, controlling the timing of each thrust.

dialogue.text: Colonial chroniclers, even hostile ones, called him bold and skilful. At Chinhat, courage was lashed to timing and terrain, turning scattered bands into a concerted blow.

i18n.hi: गोरखानी इतिहासकार, दुश्मन होते हुए भी, उसे दिलेर और हुनरमंद लिखते हैं। चिनहट में बहादुरी, समय और ज़मीन से बंध गई, बिखरी टोलियों को एक साथ प्रहार में बदलते हुए।

panels.shot: chaotic mid-shot of British troops falling back in disorder
panels.action: British-led infantry scramble back along the road, some abandoning carts and guns; officers shout orders, while distant Lucknow domes shimmer through the haze of gun smoke.

dialogue.text: Under fire, short of water, flanked and outnumbered, Lawrence’s men fell back in disorder. Chinhat became one of the revolt’s few clear open-field defeats for the Company.

i18n.hi: गोलीबारी में, पानी की कमी में, चारों तरफ से घिरकर और कम संख्या में, लॉरेंस के लोग अफरातफरी में पीछे हटे। चिनहट कंपनी के लिए गिनती की खुली मैदान की साफ हारों में से एक बना।

panels.shot: wide shot of the battered column racing back toward the Residency
panels.action: The remnants of the column hurry toward the Lucknow Residency, some men stumbling alongside gun carriages, the city walls looming as black smoke rises beyond.

dialogue.text: The beaten force fled to the Residency. Chinhat’s loss pushed the British into a long siege in Lucknow and turned Ahmadullah Shah into a feared commander in their reports.

i18n.hi: हारी हुई टुकड़ी रेज़िडेंसी की तरफ भागी। चिनहट की हार ने अंग्रेज़ों को लखनऊ में लम्बी घेराबंदी में धकेल दिया और उनकी नज़र में अहमदुल्लाह शाह को डरावना सरदार बना दिया।

panels.shot: somber interior shot of Henry Lawrence wounded on a cot
panels.action: Inside a darkened Residency room days later, Henry Lawrence lies on a cot, bandaged, officers gathered around as a shell hole in the wall reveals a faint plume of smoke outside.

dialogue.text: On 4 July, a shell wounded Lawrence inside the besieged Residency. He died soon after, his decision at Chinhat tied forever to Lucknow’s grim months of resistance.

i18n.hi: 4 जुलाई को घिरी रेज़िडेंसी के भीतर एक गोला लॉरेंस को घायल कर गया। थोड़े ही समय बाद वह मर गया, चिनहट का उसका फैसला हमेशा के लिए लखनऊ की कड़वी घेराबंदी से जुड़ गया।

panels.shot: wide shot of rebels around Lucknow, Ahmadullah among them
panels.action: Around Lucknow’s outskirts, rebel bands gather in makeshift camps; Ahmadullah Shah rides through one, exchanging brief words with other leaders, the battered city in the far background.

dialogue.text: Ahmadullah Shah fought as part of a broad Awadh coalition. His authority came from faith and fury, but also from movement—linking scattered fronts, refusing to let the revolt shrink to one city.

i18n.hi: अहमदुल्लाह शाह एक बड़े अवध गठजोड़ का हिस्सा होकर लड़े। उनकी ताकत ईमान और ग़ुस्से से आती थी, लेकिन चलने–फिरने से भी—मोरचे जोड़ते हुए, बगावत को एक शहर में सिमटने से रोकते हुए।

panels.shot: transitional map-style shot dissolving into countryside march
panels.action: A faded map of northern Awadh and Rohilkhand overlays into a live scene of Ahmadullah Shah’s contingent marching through fields near Shahjahanpur, banners fluttering.

dialogue.text: After Lucknow fell, British armies spread across Awadh. Ahmadullah Shah moved northward, fighting around Shahjahanpur, the struggle now a war of survival and shifting allies.

i18n.hi: लखनऊ गिरने के बाद अंग्रेज़ी फौजें अवध में फैल गईं। अहमदुल्लाह शाह उत्तर की ओर बढ़े, शाहजहाँपुर के आस–पास लड़ते हुए, लड़ाई अब ज़िंदा रहने और बदलते साथियों की जंग थी।

panels.shot: tense medium shot of Ahmadullah meeting the Raja of Powayan
panels.action: In the courtyard of a small fort at Powayan, Ahmadullah Shah stands, composed, before the Raja of Powayan seated on a low throne, retainers watching from the shadows.

dialogue.text: British records tell of a final turn: negotiations and proximity to the Raja of Powayan, a local chief balancing fear of rebel repute against the lure of Company reward.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ी कागज़ों में आखिरी मोड़ लिखा है: पवाँयां के राजा से बातचीत, एक छोटा सरदार जो बगावती नाम के डर और कंपनी इनाम के लोभ के बीच तौल–मोल कर रहा था।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of the Raja’s retainers closing in from behind
panels.action: In the same courtyard, Powayan retainers step quietly behind Ahmadullah Shah, hands near their weapons, while the Raja watches, expression unreadable, under the heavy summer sky.

dialogue.text: On 5 June 1858, the Raja’s men killed and beheaded Ahmadullah Shah. For this, the British paid him fifty thousand silver pieces, recorded in their own official accounts.

i18n.hi: 5 जून 1858 को राजा के लोगों ने अहमदुल्लाह शाह को मारकर सिर काट दिया। इसके बदले अंग्रेज़ों ने उसे पचास हज़ार चाँदी के सिक्के दिए, जो उनके अपने सरकारी कागज़ों में दर्ज हैं।

panels.shot: somber close-up of a British officer counting silver coins
panels.action: Close on British hands stacking shimmering silver coins on a wooden table inside a cantonment tent, a written receipt beside them naming the Raja of Powayan and the sum.

dialogue.text: The Maulvi of Faizabad fell not on a field, but by a bargain. The Company listed his death neatly among payments and reports; his scattered followers carried only the story.

i18n.hi: फैज़ाबाद के मौलवी को मैदान नहीं, सौदे पर गिराया गया। कंपनी ने उसकी मौत को हिसाब–किताब और रिपोर्टों की कतार में साफ–सुथरा दर्ज कर लिया; उसके बचे–खुचे साथियों के पास बस किस्सा रह गया।

panels.shot: epic low-angle silhouette of Ahmadullah Shah on horseback against dusk
panels.action: A stylized silhouette of Ahmadullah Shah on horseback crests a hill at dusk, Chinhat’s fields fading behind him into the long roads of Awadh, the sky streaked with deep orange.

dialogue.text: Ahmadullah Shah’s arc from Faizabad to Chinhat and Powayan shows how revolt rests on both faith and foresight—on men who can turn raw courage into a plan, and accept that even victory can lead toward a scaffold.

i18n.hi: फैज़ाबाद से चिनहट और पवाँयां तक अहमदुल्लाह शाह की यात्रा दिखाती है कि बगावत ईमान और दूरदर्शी दिमाग—दोनों पर टिकती है; ऐसे लोगों पर जो निडरता को योजना में ढाल सकें, और ये भी मान लें कि जीत भी कभी–कभी फाँसी के रास्ते ले जाती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Ahmadullah Shah and the Trap at Chinhat
subtitle_i18n.hi: अहमदुल्लाह शाह और चिनहट का जाल
